title: VWAP from a Trade Tape

statement.md: The Volume-Weighted Average Price of a set of trades is the total notional traded divided by the total volume traded. Execution desks benchmark their fills against VWAP all day: buying below VWAP is good, buying above VWAP is slippage. Given a trade tape, your job is to compute VWAP exactly.

statement.caption: q_i = quantity (shares) of trade i, p_i = price of trade i

statement.md: Real prices are quoted with at most two decimal places (cents). To keep the arithmetic exact, this feed gives every price as an *integer number of cents*, 1234 means 12.34, and every quantity as an integer number of shares. Compute everything in integers; never let the accumulation pass through floating point.

Read n trades, each on its own line as two integers: quantity then price-in-cents. Print the VWAP in dollars with exactly 4 digits after the decimal point, rounded to nearest (ties to even). No test has an exact halfway case, so any correct rounding of the exact rational value is accepted.

statement.title: Why integers and not floats?
statement.md: A product like 100000 cents x 10000 shares is 10^9, and summing 10^5 of them approaches 10^14. Sums below 2^53 happen to be exactly representable in a double, but nothing in the problem guarantees that margin in general, and the division introduces rounding you do not control. Accumulating p*q and q as exact 64-bit integers and dividing once is exact by construction. This scaled-integer trick (read 2-decimal prices as integer cents) is standard practice in production trading systems.

inputFormat: Line 1: the integer n. Each of the next n lines contains two integers separated by a space: q (shares, 1 <= q <= 10^4) and p (price in integer cents, 1 <= p <= 10^5).
outputFormat: One line: the VWAP in dollars with exactly 4 digits after the decimal point. VWAP in cents is (sum of p*q) / (sum of q); divide by 100 to get dollars. Example: a VWAP of 1224 cents prints as 12.2400.
constraints: 1 <= q_i <= 10^4 (shares) and 1 <= p_i <= 10^5 (cents, i.e. price below 1000.00)
The total notional sum of p_i * q_i is at most 10^14 and the total share count is at most 10^9, both fit in a signed 64-bit integer.
Output is rounded to 4 decimal places, round half to even; no test value lies exactly on a halfway point.

examples.explanation: Notional = 1234*100 + 1200*200 + 1300*50 = 428400 (cents x shares); volume = 350 shares. VWAP = 428400/350 = 1224 cents = 12.2400 dollars.

hints: Keep two running integer sums: notional = sum of p*q and volume = sum of q. Both fit in 64-bit integers under the constraints.
VWAP in dollars = notional / (volume * 100). To print 4 decimals exactly, scale first: VWAP * 10000 = notional * 100 / volume, one exact integer division plus a remainder.

Round using the remainder: if 2*remainder > divisor round up; if 2*remainder == divisor round half to even (increment only when the quotient is odd). Then print quotient/10000 as the integer part and quotient%10000 zero-padded to 4 digits.

editorial.text: Approach: scaled-integer arithmetic end to end

editorial.md: The only trap in this problem is numerical. Do the whole computation in integers and convert to a printable decimal string at the very last step, by hand.

editorial.title: Worked derivation
items: Accumulate notional = sum p_i q_i (integer cents times shares) and volume = sum q_i. Under the constraints notional <= 10^14 and volume <= 10^9, so both fit comfortably in signed 64-bit.
We must print VWAP rounded to 4 decimals, i.e. round( VWAP * 10000 ). Since VWAP * 10000 = notional * 100 / volume, form num = notional * 100 (<= 10^16, still safe in 64-bit) and den = volume.
Integer-divide: q4 = num / den, rem = num % den. The exact value is q4 + rem/den.
Round half to even: if 2*rem > den, use q4 + 1; if 2*rem == den, use q4 + 1 only when q4 is odd; otherwise keep q4.
Print q4 / 10000, a dot, and (q4 % 10000) zero-padded to 4 digits. All values here are non-negative, so floor division matches mathematical division.

editorial.md: Example: trades 250 @ 98.76, 10 @ 99.00, 1000 @ 100.00, 40 @ 99.99 give notional = 12967960 and volume = 1300. num/den = 1296796000 / 1300 = 997535 remainder 500; 2*500 = 1000 < 1300 so no round-up: the answer is 997535 scale units = 99.7535 dollars.
Complexity: $O(n)$ time, $O(1)$ extra memory. Any language's 64-bit integers suffice; there is no need for big integers or floating point anywhere.

editorial.title: Where this shows up in real systems
editorial.md: Trade capture and TCA (transaction cost analysis) pipelines accumulate notional and volume as integers (cents x shares) for exactly this reason: a day of ticks must produce a bit-identical VWAP on every replay. Float accumulation makes replays ordering-dependent; integer accumulation does not.

solutions.python:
import sys


def main():
    tok = sys.stdin.buffer.read().split()
    n = int(tok[0])
    notional = shares = 0
    for i in range(n):
        q = int(tok[1 + 2 * i])
        p = int(tok[2 + 2 * i])
        notional += q * p
        shares += q
    # VWAP in units of 1e-4 dollars is 100 * notional / shares; round to nearest in exact integers.
    units = (200 * notional + shares) // (2 * shares)
    print(f"{units // 10000}.{units % 10000:04d}")


main()
